model_annotation: This bar chart illustrates the “effect” of six different language models—mBERT-L₂, XLM-L₂, mBERT-R₂, XLM-R₂, mBERT-B₂, and XLM-B₂—across nine language families or categories: IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic family, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic. The vertical y-axis, labeled “effect,” ranges from 0 to 30 with major gridlines at intervals of 10, and each bar is accompanied by error bars indicating variability or confidence intervals. The horizontal x-axis lists the language categories in a fixed order, not sorted by magnitude. Within each category, the six models are represented by distinct colored bars: light blue (mBERT-L₂), dark blue (XLM-L₂), light green (mBERT-R₂), dark green (XLM-R₂), light pink (mBERT-B₂), and red (XLM-B₂), as indicated by the legend in the upper right. The effect values vary widely: for example, in IE-Indic, XLM-B₂ reaches approximately 21, while mBERT-L₂ is near 0; in Semitic, XLM-B₂ peaks around 20, whereas mBERT-R₂ is near -2. In contrast, for Uralic and Isolate categories, most models show near-zero or slightly negative effects. The chart visually emphasizes that model performance (effect) is highly dependent on both the model architecture and the language family, with some models (notably XLM-B₂ and mBERT-B₂) consistently showing higher effects in several Indo-European branches, while others (like mBERT-L₂ and XLM-L₂) perform more moderately or variably.
